claim: Executive control is several related parts, not one module: inhibition, shifting and updating correlate (latent r .42-.63) but are separable; a common factor plus specific factors fits best.
agent_test: Run separate probes (switch, hold/update, filter) on the agent and check that gains on one do not predict gains on the others.

claim: A single 'inhibition' ability is not a stable, measurable trait: inhibition tasks barely correlate with each other and the factor is poorly supported; stop-type and filter-type failures look separate.
schema_part: none (do not add an inhibition operator; schema 4b)
agent_test: Compare a combined 'ignore' guard against separate stop-type and filter-type guards at equal tokens.

claim: Classic conflict-task difference scores are unreliable for individual differences (test-retest ICC .14-.82; Stroop RT cost .60-.66, flanker .40-.57). One-run deltas on an agent are noise.
agent_test: Score switch or interference cost as paired item-level differences over many items and repeats; report the spread.

claim: Count-based error measures (go/no-go commission errors ICC .76) are steadier than timing deltas, so counted checks beat timed ones.
agent_test: Compare split-half reliability of an error-count score vs a token-length score on the same agent runs.

claim: Anxiety reduces attentional control in humans (g about -0.58, k=58, N=8292), mainly efficiency (RT) more than accuracy, in inhibition and switching but not updating, and more under high load.
agent_test: Test whether pressure wording raises token use before it lowers accuracy on a fixed task set.

claim: Anxiety also lowers working-memory capacity (g about -.33, k=177, N=22,061; -.31 without outliers); the effect is modest with high heterogeneity (I2 67%).
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as an upper bound on the effect size to expect from wording changes.

claim: Worry content, not arousal or anxiety as such, may carry the cost: worry g -.45 vs arousal -.33; worry predicts low common EF (beta -.43) while anxiety latent r is near 0.
agent_test: Add worry-like self-referential caution text to a scaffold prompt vs a matched neutral text; compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Evidence on updating under anxiety conflicts: Shi 2019 finds no updating deficit; Moran finds the largest loss on dynamic (n-back style) span (g -.437), while the Moran supplement lists dynamic at -.29.
agent_test: Not tested on the agent; unresolved human-side question.
gap_note: Likely task-coding difference (capacity vs efficiency); moderator tables not accessible, unresolved.

claim: ACT predictions are supported mainly by small studies; no large preregistered replication was found, and some recent studies give null results (N=71, BF01 about 1.6-1.8) or task-dependence.
agent_test: Treat any ACT-derived scaffold rule as a hypothesis; A/B it on our harness.
gap_note: No large preregistered ACT replication found; CO2-induced anxiety left goal-directed control unchanged (N=88, 50, 1413).

claim: Practice or training on one control task does not transfer: Stroop practice cut conflict time 34% but left interference; adolescent WM training did not beat control (p=.22).
agent_test: Check that a warm-up or few-shot conflict drill in the prompt does not improve a different conflict task.

claim: In LLMs, irrelevant context costs accuracy (flanker analogue): under 30% of base problems stay solved after one distractor sentence; near-miss distractors (role overlap, in-range numbers) hurt most.
agent_test: Insert near-miss vs off-topic distractors into agent inputs; compare with and without a code filter at equal tokens, on current models.
gap_note: Gap 5: near-miss text still hurts 2024-2026 setups (up to 65% drop; ghost-context 38.3%); a code-side mask of the top distractor recovered 95.5% of detected errors. Two of the three sources are abstract-only.

claim: A short 'ignore irrelevant context' instruction gives small gains (CoT micro 72.4 to 77.8); sampling plus voting gives larger ones (+11 micro points; correct answer in the 20 samples for 99.7%) but best macro stays 45%. Selection in code beats telling the model to ignore.
agent_test: Compare instruction-only, filter-in-code and vote-of-N arms at equal tokens on a distractor set.

claim: LLM proactive interference: retrieval of the latest value declines log-linearly toward zero as overwritten updates accumulate (3-400 per key), even with input length held constant; 'ignore earlier input' prompts help only a little. Remove stale text instead of asking the model to inhibit it.
agent_test: Compare a context that keeps stale versions plus an 'outdated' note against one with stale versions removed, at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap 4: slope is model-specific and size-driven (context window length not significant); forget/ignore prompts give marginal gains, a hard mock-QA boundary helps; fewer tracked items helps.

claim: Multi-turn carry-over is the LLM switching cost: average 39% drop (abstract; Fig 1 says -35%; 90% to 65% is 25 points) mostly from unreliability (+112%) with aptitude -15/16%; the drop appears even in 2-turn conversations; later answers bloat; wrong early assumptions persist.
agent_test: Same task: carry-on history after a wrong step vs one rebuilt consolidated prompt; compare success and run-to-run spread at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gupta 2024 adds a second, independent switch-cost source: old-task history lowers accuracy on a new task in many of 15 switches (old models).

claim: Restating all prior information each turn (SNOWBALL) recovers only 15-20% of the multi-turn loss; one complete prompt (CONCAT) scores near single-turn. Lower temperature does not cure drift in sharded runs.
agent_test: Test SNOWBALL-style restatement vs fresh rebuild inside the scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models do not escape the multi-turn loss (o3, R1 similar) and give 33% longer replies; longer replies carry more assumptions and performance is 10-50% higher in the shortest-reply conditions on 5 of 6 tasks.
agent_test: Cap reply length per attempt and compare to uncapped at equal total tokens.

claim: Classic Stroop run on frontier LLMs: incongruent accuracy collapses as list length grows (GPT-4o 91% at 5 words to 15% at 40; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 76% at 20 to 24% at 40) while word reading stays about 99%; no reliable congruency-sequence effect. Peer-reviewed (Patel, Wang, Fan; PNAS Nexus 2026), n=30 per primary model; later models tested at n=5 only.
schema_part: S3/G11 (keep contexts short; split conflict items in code)
agent_test: Re-run the list-length Stroop on our model; then test whether splitting the list into short chunks in code removes the collapse.
gap_note: Corrected: the Stroop stimuli were images, not text; newer models n=5 still show deficits; cause of Claude vs GPT-4o gap untested.

claim: Emotional framing moves LLM behaviour: anxious preprompts raise self-reported anxiety in all models tested vs neutral and bias scores rose (beta .62 anxious, .71 neutral preprompt; STICSA adds beta .08); effect is model-specific and a neutral preamble is not a safe control. This is prompt-wording sensitivity, not proven anxiety.
agent_test: Compare neutral, urgent and calming scaffold preambles on our model at equal tokens.

claim: A calming prompt after a distressing context only partly resets a model (GPT-4 STAI-s: 30.8 baseline, 67.8 after trauma, 44.4 after relaxation); a fresh context is cleaner than talking the old one down.
agent_test: After a hostile or failed context, compare 'calm it down' text vs fresh rebuild on next-task accuracy.
gap_note: Shnaidman 2026: history-keeping repairs recover 2-3 of 14 pairs, deleting the history 14 of 14.

claim: Positive or negative emotional prompt text can both raise benchmark scores (EmotionPrompt +8% / +115% relative; NegativePrompt +12.89% / +46.25%), so effects reflect wording sensitivity, not an ACT mechanism, and need equal-token tests.
agent_test: Run EmotionPrompt-style suffixes against equal-length neutral padding.

claim: Updating load degrades with n for LLMs (n-back d' about 1 at n=3 for gpt-3.5-turbo; added noise lowers capacity), so keep per-step load small.
agent_test: Run an n-back probe on our model before deciding attempt length.

claim: Longer or padded contexts and extended reasoning can hurt: reasoning degrades well below the maximum input length; middle-of-context information is used worse; chain-of-thought can reduce accuracy on some tasks (o1-preview 57.7% vs GPT-4o 94.0% on an implicit-learning subset).
agent_test: Compare short-thinking vs long-thinking arms at equal tokens on a distractor-heavy set.

claim: Switch cost depends on expected switch rate: in a model and human reanalysis, frequent-switch contexts shrink the cost; high-anxiety humans re-learn a context rule poorly after a flip (CSPC -4 ms vs 30 ms, N=54).
agent_test: Flip a task rule mid-run; compare re-learning in the same context vs a fresh one.
gap_note: Human environment-specific flexibility needed 4 days of training (N=51); 1 day failed (N=52). In-context adaptation is the transient kind only.

claim: Self-correction in the same context without outside feedback often fails or worsens answers; the model's own opinion is a weak trigger for a set shift.
agent_test: Compare same-context self-revision with revision triggered by an external check, at equal tokens.

claim: Cognitive-architecture accounts (Stroop PDP, conflict monitoring, task-set inertia, supervisory system) back a control signal plus a lingering old task set, but were not opened in this run.
agent_test: Not directly testable; background only.

claim: Delete-and-rebuild beats keep-and-repair: after false pressure in a conversation, repairs that keep the history recover 2-3 of 14 model-dataset pairs; removing the history recovers 14 of 14. A fake closed turn (mock QA reset) helps proactive interference, a spoken 'new session' note does not.
agent_test: Compare, at equal tokens, a rebuilt context against history plus an 'ignore' or retraction note on our agent.

claim: The Stroop list-length collapse is shown only for image lists in two vision-language models (n=30 per cell) plus n=5 checks on three newer models; whether it appears in text, or after chunking, is untested.
agent_test: Run a text-only Stroop list at 5/10/20/40 words on our model, then the same items chunked in code.

claim: Interference resistance is a measurable per-model slope (IES) that depends on model size, not on context window length; the number of concurrently tracked items and the length of each item drive it more than anything a prompt can say.
agent_test: Measure our model's key-value interference curve and set the forced-reset step count where accuracy hits a chosen floor.

claim: A code-side filter (mask the top-attributed distractor span) recovers about 95% of detected context-misattribution errors with little collateral damage in one small study.
agent_test: Run a mask-and-rerun filter on our agent inputs; track fixes versus collateral damage.

claim: Direct LLM switch-cost tests are few and old: Gupta 2024 (4 models) shows many task switches lower accuracy; two WCST-on-LLM papers (2025) were found by title only; no flanker or cued task-switching test with measured switch cost on 2025-2026 models was found.
agent_test: Read the two WCST papers; then run a cued switch task on our model with and without a fresh context.

claim: Frequent-switch exposure produces lasting flexibility in humans only after multi-day practice (4 days yes, 1 day no) and in a recurrent network through slow weight change; a no-training scaffold has only the transient in-context part.
agent_test: No test needed; do not expect a benefit from frequent resets to accumulate.
